Q1: Should this fix also make the `test_closed_reader_does_not_rerun_a_successful_command` failure pass, even though `agents.md` is the only file the issue lists?
Choices:
A: Only regenerate `agents.md` with `make generate`. Handle the gh_retry test in a separate issue, since it likely fails for every PR on ubuntu-26.04. The PR #9359 CI stays red until that fix lands.
B: Regenerate `agents.md` and fix the gh_retry closed-reader test in the same change on `ai/issue-9342`, so the PR's CI goes green in this generation. (RECOMMENDED)
C: Only regenerate `agents.md` and re-run CI to check whether the gh_retry test is flaky before doing anything else.
Q2: If the gh_retry test is in scope (Q1:B), how should it be fixed? (Ignore if Q1 is A or C.)
Choices:
A: Make the test work on any host. Keep its intent and its non-zero-status check, but use a reader that closes its input at once (as the `cat_closed` probe does, which gets 141 on these runners) instead of `head -c 1`. `scripts/gh_helpers.sh` stays unchanged. (RECOMMENDED)
B: Change how `gh_retry` passes on the output of a successful command (`scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1227-1231`, plus the two inline copies in `review_autofix.yml` if they need it) so a reader that drains the output early is still reported as non-zero on Rust coreutils. Keep the test as it is.
C: Skip or xfail the test on hosts running Rust coreutils (uutils). **Note:** this weakens a contract test, which the issue and repo rules discourage.
